answer.question: Are we on pace to hit goal, and where do we land by election day if nothing changes?
answer.answer:
Program-wide we're ahead of where we should be right now, but if nothing changes we finish about 3,300 doors short — Northside is the only office with a cushion.

- Program (All offices): 33,503 doors vs 32,431 goal to date, 103.3% of goal to date, but projected 57,329 vs a 60,632 goal — 3,303 short, 94.6% of goal [view:v_office_pace]
- Eastgate: 8,505 doors vs 9,521 goal to date (89.3%) and projected 14,596 vs 17,800 — 3,204 short (82%) [view:v_office_pace]
- Harbor: 11,351 vs 10,782 to date (105.3%) but projected 19,150 vs 20,157 — 1,007 short (95%) [view:v_office_pace]
- Northside: 13,647 vs 12,128 to date (112.5%) and projected 23,583 vs 22,675 — 908 over (104%) [view:v_office_pace]
- To close the gap: the program needs 33.3 shifts a day vs 29.3 actually run, i.e. 4.1 extra shifts per day; Eastgate alone needs 4.4 more [view:v_office_pace]

Method: projection = doors to date + average daily doors of the last 7 days (Oct 12–18) × the 16 knocking days left, Oct 19 to Nov 3 [doc:program-plan#pace-and-projection].

answer.question: Based on our pace and what's left, should we ask the client for more doors, or a second pass on the turf we have?
answer.answer:
Ask the client for more doors — new first-pass turf — because at our current rate we'll run out of untouched turf before Election Day; a second pass is only the fallback.

- Remaining capacity: 1,489.1 average daily doors × 16 knocking days left = 23,825.6 doors of capacity left [table:v_office_pace]
- Untouched doors left in our turf: 10,393 of 41,853 target doors [table:v_precinct_coverage]
- So capacity is well over twice the untouched turf (23,825.6 vs 10,393) — we run out of first-pass turf [doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass]
- By office, capacity vs untouched: Northside 9,936 vs 1,114, Eastgate 6,091.2 vs 1,183 — both clearly short of turf; Harbor is the exception at 7,798.4 vs 8,096 untouched, so Harbor can keep working what it has [table:v_precinct_coverage] [table:v_office_pace]
- We are also behind overall: projected 57,329 vs goal 60,632, a shortfall of 3,303 (94.6% of goal), needing 4.1 extra shifts per day [table:v_office_pace]

Method: the plan says to compare average daily doors of the last 7 days times days left against untouched doors — if capacity is larger, ask for more doors first, because new turf contacts at the normal first-pass rate while second passes contact at roughly half that rate [doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass].

cases.question: What counts as flash knocking under our QC rules?

answer.question: What counts as flash knocking under our QC rules?
answer.answer:
Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock: a shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking].

- Threshold: 10+ consecutive knocks less than 30 seconds apart on a shift [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Confirmed cases are rolled back: the knocks in the flagged window stop counting as doors or contacts, and a whole shift recorded that way is rolled back in full [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Rolled-back knocks stay in the data with rolled_back = true, and never change a client report already sent [doc:counting-doors#rollbacks]
- Every open flag needs a field lead–canvasser conversation before the canvasser's next shift; two or more householding or flash knocking flags in one week go to the field director [doc:qc-rules#what-happens-after-a-flag]

cases.question: How should a canvasser record a locked apartment building?

answer.question: How should a canvasser record a locked apartment building?
answer.answer:
Record the locked building once as "inaccessible" on its first unit, then move on — don't mark every unit.

- Locked building: record it once as "inaccessible" on its first unit [doc:qc-rules#apartments-and-units]
- Every apartment unit is still its own door and must be knocked individually [doc:qc-rules#apartments-and-units]
- Marking a whole building from the lobby counts as householding, a QC flag [doc:qc-rules#apartments-and-units]
- Hosting every unit instead: an attempt is one knock record, while a door is one address unit knocked on one day [doc:counting-doors#attempts] [doc:counting-doors#doors]

How it works: a door is one address unit (a house or one apartment unit) knocked on one day, so the locked entry is logged as a single "inaccessible" attempt on the first unit rather than a pass for each unit behind the locked door [doc:counting-doors#doors].
